task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: separating role coverage from talent and counts
causal inference of talent control on coverage
evidence_does_not_establish: no prior empirical findings on lineup structural role coverage
no evidence that talent control can be isolated from counts
own_inferences: The task references structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal) but no prior study in the repository has operationalized or validated these categories in NBA data; thus the concept is novel within this research set.

The data set contains sufficient possessions and seasons to estimate correlations, but measuring structural role coverage itself is a methodological challenge that has not been addressed by existing studies.
uncertainties: Whether the play‑by‑play and possession graph can be used to reliably label players as organizer, shaper, or terminal in a reproducible way.
Whether talent and count controls can be adequately specified to isolate the effect of coverage.

historical_effect.explanation: No past evidence was retrieved; the decision will be based solely on data availability and methodological feasibility.

blocking_constraints.text: Need a validated method to assign structural roles to players based on possession data; current data do not provide role labels.
Talent, player minutes, and game context may confound any observed association between coverage and performance.
Effect sizes for structural role coverage may be small, requiring larger samples than the 90 team‑seasons provide for robust causal inference.

prior_work.summary: No prior studies in the repository have addressed the specific question of lineup structural role coverage and its separability from talent/counts.

risks.text: Structural role labels are not directly observed; any derived metric may be noisy.
Talent and minutes may drive both coverage and outcomes.
Limited ability to detect small but meaningful effects.
The possession graph may omit subtle interactions critical for defining roles.

design.estimand: Effect of the proportion of lineup minutes covered by at least one organizer, shaper, or terminal on team winning percentage, controlling for team talent and player count metrics.
design.sample: All NBA games from 2022‑23 through 2025‑26 playoffs (420,993 possessions, 90 team‑seasons).
design.power: We would require ~200 team‑seasons to achieve 80% power for a small (Cohen’s d≈0.2) effect; current sample is below that threshold for causal inference.
design.controls: Team‑level talent rating (e.g., adjusted plus/minus or player efficiency rating weighted by minutes), total player minutes per game, and game context variables (home/away, opponent strength).
design.falsification: Check whether the same effect holds when roles are randomly permuted within lineups; a null result would support causal inference.
design.multiplicity: Multiple role definitions (organizer, shaper, terminal) and multiple seasons (fixed vs. random effects) increase the family‑wise error; adjust significance with Bonferroni or false discovery rate.
design.decision_rule: Reject the null if p<0.05 after adjustment; otherwise conclude no evidence for an effect.
